feature: The first window after launch opens as quickly as the ones after it
summary: The first capture or recording you open after the app starts no longer waits about a third of a second longer than later ones. The app now builds the editor out of sight while it launches, so a recording opened the moment you press Stop shows its last frame in about a quarter of a second, even when it is the first thing you open.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: a-recording-opens-at-stop-walk (no flags), and the same walk without its first step to time the first window of a run.

try.do: Quit Photonz and start it again from the Dock or Spotlight.
Press Shift Command 5 and record a few seconds of the screen.
Stop the recording and click Edit on the corner card straight away.
Close the window, record again and open it the same way, and compare how quickly each window showed its picture.
Quit and relaunch, then open a screenshot from Capture History first, to check a picture opens just as quickly.

evaluate: Does the first recording you open after launch now feel as quick as the second?
Does anything flash, appear in the Dock or show up in the Window menu while the app starts?
Is the app quick to answer its capture keys straight after launch, or do you notice it settling for a moment?
rough: Measured with the open-at-stop walk, eight runs each, Stop to the picture: the first window of a run took 438 to 614 ms before and 174 to 325 ms now (mean 241). A window opened beside one already open takes 149 to 179 ms (mean 167).

A window opened when no other editor window is open still costs about 100 ms more than one opened beside an open window (159 to 325 ms, mean 266, for a second window after closing the first). That is the app turning from a menu-bar icon into a Dock app, and it is the same for the first window of a run and any later one, so the warm-up cannot buy it back without putting an icon in the Dock.
Launch takes about a third of a second longer, spent building the hidden editor before the app answers its first key.

No picture attached: every capture this walk takes is a recording of a corner of the live screen, which on this run showed the person's own browser, so the pictures stay in /tmp/photonz-playtest/a-recording-opens-at-stop-walk rather than going into the repo. Nothing on screen changes with this work, only how soon it appears.
